subject.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers

question: Should OpenClaw accept the narrow fail-closed same-label system LaunchDaemon policy, including refusal on unverifiable ownership, as the compatibility tradeoff for preventing duplicate gateway managers?
rationale: The patch is a focused fix with convincing proof, but it intentionally stops workflows that previously proceeded when a system job, stale plist, or permissions ambiguity existed; that operator-policy choice belongs to maintainers.

options.title: Accept the narrow guard
options.body: Merge after rebase and green gates, treating system-domain ownership or unverifiable state as a hard stop before user LaunchAgent mutation or activation.

options.title: Narrow unverifiable failures
options.body: Require only confirmed ownership conflicts to stop the workflow and define a different warning or recovery policy for probe and filesystem errors.

options.title: Wait for unified lifecycle design
options.body: Pause this PR until system and user launchd install, status, restart, stop, uninstall, and privilege UX share one deliberate contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow guard
recommendation.body: Merge after rebase and green gates, treating system-domain ownership or unverifiable state as a hard stop before user LaunchAgent mutation or activation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned, contributed the activation-conflict implementation, and have the strongest recent history on this launchd decision surface.
